listening.title: The candidate asks the last questions

lines.speaker: Thu (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Khanh, we are almost finished. Do you have any questions for us?

lines.speaker: Khanh (Candidate)
lines.text: Yes, thank you. What does success look like in my first 90 days?

lines.speaker: Thu (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: You should ship one small feature and understand our main product by then.

lines.speaker: Khanh (Candidate)
lines.text: That is clear. Which success metrics does the team follow every quarter?

lines.speaker: Thu (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Delivery speed, the bug rate after release, and feedback from internal users.

lines.speaker: Khanh (Candidate)
lines.text: Could you tell me more about the tech stack your team uses today?

lines.speaker: Thu (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Mostly Java and React, with a slow move towards a cloud platform.

lines.speaker: Khanh (Candidate)
lines.text: Good to know. May I ask about the remote policy and the training budget?

lines.speaker: Thu (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Two days from home each week, and every engineer has a yearly training budget.

lines.speaker: Khanh (Candidate)
lines.text: One last question: what is the typical career path for this role?

lines.speaker: Thu (Hiring Manager)
lines.text: Senior in about two years, then technical lead if the performance review cycle goes well.

lines.speaker: Khanh (Candidate)
lines.text: Thank you. Could you also share who will join the interview panel next round?
